passage:
In summer, City High School felt hotter every year. The science club used small thermometers to measure different places on campus.
They found that the parking lot was much hotter than the garden. The basketball court was hotter than the shaded hallway. Dark ground held more heat than grass.
The students made a heat map and showed it to the principal. They suggested planting trees, painting some roofs lighter, and adding shade near waiting areas.
Their report did not solve the heat problem immediately, but it helped people see it clearly.
Numbers turned complaints into evidence. The sun was the same, but the surfaces below it changed how much students suffered.
